title: Review of pcell yield selection (finding): replicated on fresh seeds 5 and 6; low-yield particles fall to 0.09-0.15 vs neutral 0.54, colonization-phase as stated
summary: Looked at selection_ts.png and kinds_y0.7_s0.png, then re-ran the author's comp.py on the published world.py for fresh seeds: y2=0.7 on seeds 5 and 6 and the neutral arm (y2=1.0) on seed 5, T=16000, plus a labkit run of the y2=0.7 world on seed 5 (rerun/seed5). Kind-1 (low-yield) particle share in cells: 0.47 -> 0.09 (seed 5) and 0.53 -> 0.15 (seed 6), against 0.47 -> 0.54 in the neutral arm; cells purify in all three runs (pure fraction 0.91, 0.82, 0.75 at t=16000), so purification is drift and the yield effect is the share. In the labkit sheet small pale cells with few particles stay small while dense cells grow into dumbbells and divide (t=7000-8300, 13200-16000); the cell count rises 26 -> 32 with no visible cell deaths, consistent with the author's colonization-phase reading. I did not rerun the genealogy (splits by parent kind) or the gate-off ablation.

observations.H: data/summary.txt: low-yield share 0.47->0.09 (seed 5), 0.53->0.15 (seed 6) vs neutral 0.47->0.54 (seed 5); rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=7000-16000: small pale cells do not divide, dense cells do

controls_run.H: data/comp_neu_s5.log: neutral arm y2=1.0 on the same seed

verdicts.limitation: As the finding says: kinds are seeded 50/50 per particle and selection happens while cells colonize free space, with no cell deaths seen; one neutral seed only. This is cell-level selection on a particle-carried phenotype, not L7.
